title: build(deps): bump three from 0.185.1 to 0.186.1
intent: Routine Dependabot currency, no advisory. three 0.185.1 -> 0.186.1 (r186) in packages/client. Authored by hand because Dependabot cannot author a manifest (CBSP21-NOBORROW-001); the payload of that friction is the lockfile audit and the r186 migration-guide check recorded in behavior_change.
behavior_change: none expected in the shipped app. Lockfile audited against merge base 5258d4c6 (= origin/main at audit time) by parsing both package-lock.json trees and comparing every `packages` entry in full, not by reading the diff view. Entry count is 412 before and 412 after. Exactly 1 node_modules entry changed: three 0.185.1 -> 0.186.1 (forward), changing only version, resolved and integrity; three has no dependencies of its own. Zero packages added, zero removed, no other entry touched. The root entry differs in one key, dependencies.three ^0.185.1 -> ^0.186.1. Consumers: two files import three. components/cam/ToolpathCanvas3D.vue is LIVE (main.ts -> router/index.ts -> views/DxfToGcodeView.vue -> ToolpathPlayer.vue -> ToolpathCanvas3D.vue, by import-graph walk); components/cam/CamBackplot3D.vue is unreachable from main.ts. r186 Migration Guide (185 -> 186) items checked against client source: Object3D.dispose() added (client has no Object3D subclasses, so no super.dispose() obligation); BufferGeometryUtils.toTrianglesDrawMode, SimplifyModifier, Source->TextureSource, Sky/SkyMesh up uniform, GTAONode, LightProbeGrid, PCFSoftShadowMap, DotScreenNode/RGBShiftNode -> 0 uses each. Release note #33939 (disposed geometry deletes its own attributes): every geometry in both files is created per object in function scope and never reused after dispose(). Runtime export surface of build/three.core.js: 3 exports added (LightShadow, RenderObjectRefreshType, TextureSource), 0 removed; every THREE.* symbol the client uses is present; examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js still exists at the imported path. Known lag, not fixed here: devDependency @types/three stays at ^0.185.4 (0.186.0 is published); the used API surface is unchanged, so this is a follow-up bump, not a defect of this PR.
